pages.text: Combat is meant to be exciting, not punishing. Bosses and dungeons are there for adventure, not to grind. If you want brutal fights, this is not the pack's focus.
The pressure comes from $(thing)survival layers$() instead. Four systems push on you over time, and each one is designed so machines can solve it. Cold Sweat is tuned gentler than its default here.

$(li)$(l:survival/temperature)Temperature$(/l): biome, altitude and weather heat or chill you. Clothing and heated rooms help.$(br)$(li)$(l:survival/thirst)Thirst$(/l): water is a need, not just a decoration.$(br)$(li)$(l:survival/seasons)Seasons$(/l): crops grow in their season.
$(li)$(l:survival/pollution)Pollution$(/l): burners and engines pollute chunks, and air scrubbers clean them up.$(br2)Each system is a puzzle your factory can answer.

Dangers also live in the new worlds. See $(l:exploration/bosses)Bosses$(/l) and $(l:exploration/structures)Structures$(/l) before exploring far, and $(l:exploration/dimensions)Dimensions$(/l) for the places those dangers wait.

$(bold)Spawn can be snowy.$() You may start in a cold biome. After the short spawn grace, Cold Sweat chills a player with no warm gear, and a freezing body takes damage. Insulated clothing and a heat source fix it, see $(l:survival/temperature)Temperature$(/l) and $(l:survival/temperature_gear)Temperature Gear$(/l).

pages.title: Fights
pages.text: Bosses and dungeon mobs are tuned to be memorable, not to wear you down. Cataclysm and Mowzie's bosses have 0.7x health and 0.75x damage.
